messages:
maria (oncall): @channel getting an influx of 503s for hosted inference in us-east around 21:12 UTC. Customer reported timeouts + 500s/503s. I can see spikes on the gateway.
support_liz: customer ticket #C-21587 — ~35% of requests returning 503 in the last 20m. Model: rw/gpt-medium-v2, qps ~120, batch size usually 8.
infra_bot: [metric alert] infra.hosted.gateway.5xx_rate > 20% for 10m; affected cluster: hosted-us-east-gpu-1.
sre_jay: looking now. Can someone paste the runner pod logs and node IDs? any recent deploys?
eng_tomas: no deploys at 20:45-21:15. grabbing logs from pod infer-runner-5c9f
eng_tomas: ```
[2026-03-17 21:12:03] infer-runner ERROR: upstream process exited: signal SIGSEGV (core dumped)
[2026-03-17 21:12:03] infer-runner INFO: last kernel call: aten::scaled_dot_product_attention
[2026-03-17 21:12:04] gpu-watchdog WARN: GPU 0 hung, initiating reset
[2026-03-17 21:12:04] nvidia-smi: Process 12345 (python) killed by signal 9 (OOM?)
[2026-03-17 21:12:05] infer-runner ERROR: OutOfMemoryError: failed to allocate 280 MiB
```
sre_jay: two things in logs: GPU hang/reset + segfault in attention kernel. Could be driver/firmware or a memory regression in runtime.
maria (oncall): any quick mitigation? customers are getting timeouts.
eng_tomas: spinning up a CPU fallback pool for the customer and routing 10% as canary. command: `rbctl route update --customer C-21587 --fallback cpu-small --percent 10`
deploy-bot: route update accepted, 10% traffic diverted to cpu-small in us-east (rid: route-cc92).
sre_jay: will cordon + drain nodes with repeated GPU resets: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-47 && kubectl drain gpu-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` to avoid repeated segfaults while we debug.
support_liz: updated customer: suggested temporary fallback and asked for repro info (their request payload, model parameters). they replied with samples and said it started after a batch size increase.
eng_tomas: repro attempt locally with batch size 16 + kv-prefetch on a test 3090 replica => reproduced SIGSEGV within ~3 requests. log shows same attention kernel crash.
sre_jay: good repro. filing infra ticket for driver/kernel interaction, assigning to infra-driver team. Ticket: INFRA-4821. include coredump and sanitized payload.
maria (oncall): summary for pager: upstream worker crashes caused 503s. likely regression when batchsize raised + kv-prefetch + driver edge-case -> GPU hang + segfault. mitigation: routed small % to CPU fallback, drained affected nodes, scheduled rolling restart of hosted-us-east-gpu-1 pool.
customer_success_ana: prepping a status note for the customer: impact window 21:12-21:50 UTC, partial mitigation in place, follow-up with root cause when INFRA-4821 closed.
sre_jay: next steps: 1) collect coredumps and kernel logs from drained nodes (already copying to s3://redwood-incidents/INFRA-4821), 2) coordinate with NV driver team for repro on exact driver/build, 3) consider temporary autoscaling throttle on batch size for hosted pool.
eng_tomas: I'll push a runtime guard to reject batch_size > 12 for the affected pool as a temporary rule. rolling config update now.
deploy-bot: config rollout started (cfg-8892) -> 3/3 hosts updated.
support_liz: customer acknowledges workaround, asked for ETA on full fix. I told them we will follow up after driver team triage.
maria (oncall): thanks everyone — keep thread updated with any new 5xx spikes. I'll move to incident channel if we escalate to Sev2.
